Subject: Integration + Identity follow-up: auth options & next steps

Hi Olivia / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight plan so we can get a sandbox integration running next week. Short version: three viable auth patterns we discussed and a recommended starting path for QuantaPay.

Summary of options we reviewed
- API keys (basic): easiest to start, but broad-scoped; requires careful rotation and KMS storage on your side. Good for initial POC.
- Service accounts + short-lived tokens (recommended): Redwood issues scoped service credentials; we support a token-broker flow or JWT exchange so apps use short-lived tokens. Keys are rotated and auditable.
- OAuth / delegated flows: best for end-user delegated access and SSO-style integrations; more upfront setup (IdP metadata, consent).

Key decisions we recommend for POC
1) Start with service account + short-lived JWTs. This gives scoped access and keeps PII off long-lived keys.
2) Integrate QuantaPay KMS (customer-managed keys) for signing/rotation where you need HSM guarantees — Redwood can support CMKs for signing auth material.
3) Enable request-level logging to your audit endpoint (we can forward logs or stream via your SIEM connector).

Attachments: I dropped a short one-pager (redwood-identity-options-onepager.pdf) and a pragmatic checklist (qp-integration-checklist.xlsx) with the minimum set of items to finish a sandbox test.

Proposed mutual action plan (owners + dates)
- By 2026-08-20: QuantaPay shares network & firewall egress ranges + CI/CD sandbox service account owner (Olivia)
- By 2026-08-25: Redwood provisions sandbox service account, enables KMS-binding, and pushes sample key rotation (Sean)
- By 2026-08-29: Run SDK quickstart and end-to-end reranker test (Marissa)
- By 2026-09-01: Security deep-dive on token lifecycle & audit logs (Dylan)

Next steps from my side today: Sean will create the sandbox service account template and a short script for rotating keys against a CMK; Marissa will prepare the SDK snippet for your engineering team to run.

Please reply if any timing or the recommended pattern is a hard stop. Happy to pivot to an API-key first POC if you need speed over controls.

Thanks,
Dylan

1) CMK / HSM support: when you say \"support CMKs for signing auth material\", do you mean Redwood can import our keys (bring-your-own-key) or will Redwood call our KMS to sign tokens on-demand? We prefer the latter (we control private keys in our vault).
2) Key rotation visibility: can we get rotation events in real time (webhook) and are rotations granular per service account?
3) Token lifetime: what TTL do you recommend for POC vs production (15m / 1h / 24h)?

Also, for the sandbox network config: we will expose a restricted egress range from our staging cluster — I’ll get the IPs by Friday. Rajiv will own the KMS/crypto answers.

Olivia —

Great questions, answered inline below. TL;DR: we can support both patterns, but calling your KMS for signing is fully supported and preferred for customers that must retain key custody.

1) CMK / HSM support: Redwood supports two modes:
   a) Proxy-signing: Redwood calls your KMS (via a secure service account you provision) to sign auth tokens on-demand. Private key material never leaves your vault.
   b) Imported-key: for customers that want lower latency and are comfortable with Redwood storing wrapped keys, we can store keys wrapped with your KMS root. This is less common for regulated customers.

2) Rotation visibility: yes — rotations are per-service-account and we emit rotation events to a webhook (or push to your SIEM). We include the rotation metadata (rotation_id, time, reason).

3) Token lifetime: for a POC 1h TTL is reasonable (balance between convenience and churn). For production we recommend 15m–1h depending on threat model; long-lived refresh tokens are not recommended for service-to-service flows.

For the 30m sync on 2026-09-01 — I’ve penciled it in. I’ll send a calendar invite and include our security engineer, Sean.

Next internal action: Sean will create a sandbox provisioning script and a KMS integration example (I’ve asked him to include both proxy-signing and wrapped-key examples). Marissa will publish the SDK snippet (Node + Python) that hits the reranker endpoint with structured output enabled.

I’ll follow up with a short Loom that walks through the checklist.

Thanks,
Dylan
